updates.summary: Regulates internet information services that use 'deep synthesis' technology, defined as the use of deep learning, virtual reality and other generative or synthetic algorithms to produce text, images, audio, video, virtual scenes and other online information (25 articles). Providers must verify users' real identities, review users' inputs and synthesised outputs, and conspicuously label content that may cause public confusion or misidentification. Providers and technical supporters must run security assessments of tools that generate or edit biometric information such as faces and voices. Providers with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity must file their algorithms.
updates.notes: Adopted at the CAC office meeting of 3 Nov 2022, signed 25 Nov 2022 and published 11 Dec 2022. Technical supporters must also complete algorithm filing by reference to the provider rules (Art. 19). Its labelling articles (Arts. 16 and 17) are built on by the 2025 Measures for Labeling AI-Generated and Synthetic Content (CN-09), which, with the mandatory standard GB 45438-2025 (CN-08), set more detailed labelling duties from 1 Sept 2025.

updates.summary: Sets rules for labelling AI-generated and synthesised content (text, images, audio, video, virtual scenes) in 14 articles. updates.notes: Signed 7 Mar 2025 and published 14 Mar 2025; effective 1 Sept 2025 (Art. 14). updates.summary: Version 2.0 of China's national AI safety governance framework. Building on version 1.0 (2024), its principles include preventing loss of control and keeping AI under human control. updates.summary: Regulates AI services that simulate a natural person's personality, thinking and communication style to provide continuing emotional interaction. It bans virtual intimate-relationship services, such as virtual relatives or partners, for minors, and requires guardian consent for under-14s and a minor mode. Providers must disclose that users are dealing with AI, remind them after every 2 hours of continuous use, guard against emotional dependence, intervene in self-harm crises, offer an easy exit and not train on sensitive interaction data without separate consent. Security assessments are due at launch, after major changes and at 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users.
updates.notes: Adopted at the third CAC office meeting of 2026 on 2 Feb 2026 with the agreement of NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR, promulgated on 10 Apr 2026 as Order No. 21, in force from 15 Jul 2026, and published in the State Council Gazette, 2026 No. 17. It has 32 articles in four chapters. Emotional interaction covers emotional care, companionship, support and similar services in text, images, audio or video; services such as intelligent customer service, knowledge Q&A, work assistants, education and scientific research that involve no continuing emotional interaction are excluded (Art. 2). Providers must file their algorithms under the algorithmic recommendation provisions (Art. 26). Violations are punished under existing laws and administrative regulations; where these have no provision, the authorities may warn, circulate criticism and order correction, and for refusal or serious cases order the service stopped and may impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to 100,000, or of RMB 100,000 to 200,000 where citizens' life or health is endangered with harmful consequences (Art. 30). It also provides for an AI sandbox security service platform for innovation and safety testing (Art. 28).

updates.title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology
updates.summary: Framework law for promoting the research, development and utilization of AI-related technology. Its basic principles require transparency in research, development and utilization, since wrongful or inappropriate use can abet crime, leaks of personal information and copyright infringement, and seek a leading role in international cooperation. The State is to analyse cases in which such use infringed citizens' rights and interests and accordingly give guidance, advice and information to R&D institutions, utilization business operators and others; set guidelines in line with international norms; and adopt an AI Basic Plan. It creates the AI Strategic Headquarters, headed by the Prime Minister.
updates.notes: Enacted 28 May 2025 and promulgated as Act No. 53 of 4 Jun 2025. Under Supplementary Provisions Article 1 it took effect on promulgation, except Chapters III and IV (AI Basic Plan and AI Strategic Headquarters), which took effect on 1 Sept 2025; Supplementary Provisions Article 2 requires the government to review the Act's enforcement. Article 7 obliges utilization business operators to cooperate with the measures of the State and local governments (協力しなければならない), while R&D institutions and citizens are to endeavour to cooperate (Articles 6 and 8); the Cabinet Office's provisional English overview renders the business duty as 'shall endeavor to cooperate'. The Act contains no penalty provisions. Both Houses attached supplementary resolutions. The AI Basic Plan (Dec 2025; second plan Jul 2026) and the Article 13 appropriateness guideline (Dec 2025) were adopted under it, and the second AI Basic Plan commits to continuously reviewing the Act.

updates.summary: Presidential decree implementing Korea's AI Basic Act, in force from 22 January 2026. It defines the defence, intelligence and police AI excluded from the Act (Art. 2), organises the National AI Strategy Committee and the AI Safety Institute, and fills in the Act's trust duties. AI business operators must give prior notice of high-impact or generative AI and may mark generative outputs in human-perceivable or machine-readable form (Art. 23). The Art. 32 safety duties apply to AI systems trained with at least 10^26 floating-point operations that use the most advanced AI technology currently in use and whose risk may broadly and seriously affect life, safety or fundamental rights (Art. 24).
updates.notes: Enacted as Presidential Decree No. 36053 on 21 Jan 2026 and in force from 22 Jan 2026 (the digital medical device part of Annex 1 from 24 Jan 2026); its addenda repeal the Regulation on the Establishment and Operation of the National AI Strategy Committee and carry the committee over. Presidential Decree No. 36506 of 20 Jul 2026, in force 21 Jul 2026, added Art. 1-2, which lists the AI-vulnerable groups of Art. 3(5) of the Act (among them people with disabilities, people aged 65 or over, recipients of basic livelihood benefits, multicultural families and North Korean defectors), and requires impact assessments to reflect them (Art. 28). Presidential Decree No. 36580 of 18 Aug 2026, in force 20 Aug 2026, made a consequential change to Art. 2. Art. 25 sets the high-impact AI confirmation procedure, with a reply within 30 days. A domestic agent is required of operators with prior-year revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more, AI-service revenue of KRW 10 billion or more, or an average of 1 million or more daily domestic users (Art. 29). MSIT guidelines under the Act cover transparency (KR-04), safety (KR-05), high-impact AI determination (KR-06), high-impact AI operator duties (KR-07) and AI impact assessment (KR-08).

updates.summary: Guidance from the Ministry of Science and ICT on the transparency duties of Article 31 of Korea's AI Basic Act: prior notice that a product or service is operated on the basis of high-impact or generative AI (para. 1); marking that outputs were generated by generative AI (para. 2); and notice or marking of deepfakes, defined as virtual sound, image or video outputs hard to distinguish from reality (text excluded), so that users clearly recognise them (para. 3). The duties fall on the operator that finally provides the product or service to users, including overseas operators affecting Korean nationals. It sets out notice channels and human-perceptible or machine-readable marking methods.
updates.notes: Released by the Ministry of Science and ICT on 22 January 2026, when the Act entered into force, under the name 'Guidance on securing AI transparency (guideline)' (인공지능 투명성 확보 안내 지침(가이드라인)); a draft had been published in September 2025. NIA posted a revised file dated 26 January 2026 and recorded a wording change to the service examples for text outputs on 27 January 2026. Under the ministry's policy of a guidance period of at least one year, fact-finding and fines under the transparency provisions are suspended during that period, and the ministry plans to keep revising the guideline. Inside a service, outputs may be marked through the user interface, but outputs that can be downloaded or shared must carry the mark in the output itself; exported deepfakes need a mark that people can perceive intuitively, while artistic and creative works may use a lighter marking that does not hinder their display or enjoyment. Where a machine-readable mark is used, users must be told at least once by text or voice. A foundation-model developer that only supplies an API is not bound; the operator that offers the service to users is. The guideline coins the term 'general outputs' for AI outputs that are not deepfakes.

updates.summary: Law of 35 articles on the research, development, provision, deployment and use of AI systems and their state management. It classifies AI systems as high, medium or low risk: providers self-classify and notify medium- and high-risk systems, and high-risk systems need a conformity assessment before use. Article 4 requires human control and the ability to intervene in all decisions and behaviour of AI systems. Article 5 encourages controlled testing of technology, risk-proportionate management and voluntary compliance mechanisms, and prioritises investment in data and computing infrastructure, safe AI, skilled people and shared AI platforms of national strategic character. Article 27 requires agencies that use AI in state management or public services, and operate a high-risk system or one with significant impact on human rights, social equity or the public interest, to prepare an impact assessment report.
